author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing shows the first page when a page below the first is asked for
summary: Asking the owner listing for a page below the first shows the error page today. It must show the first page of the listing instead, and the request must succeed.
acceptance_criteria: Given owners to list, when the listing is asked for with a page below the first, then the first page of the listing is shown and the request succeeds.
Given a last name matching more than one owner, when a page below the first is asked for, then the first page of matches is shown and the request succeeds.
Given a zero page and given a negative page, when either is asked for, then each is treated as the first page (docs/prd.md Owner records edge case 4).
Given a page from the first onward, when it is asked for, then the listing behaves as it does today.
non_goals: The veterinarian directory, which shows the same failure - recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md, not scoped here
A page value that is not a number - recorded as an open question in docs/prd.md
A page beyond the last page, which already succeeds with an empty listing
Any change to how the error page itself renders (REQ-SYS-002)
notes: Boundary check: no existing requirement or Non-Goals row covers a page value outside the range, so this is an unspecified case rather than a contradiction - no owner consultation needed and no scope_overrides. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log. The owner asked for the cause to be found; the fix shape is the implementer's call.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Durable memory covers this unchanged. system-design.md Overview records that request handling and business rules sit in the controllers with no service layer, and the Contracts row for OwnerController already names server-rendered owner search with paging. Normalizing an out-of-range page parameter is that recorded shape applied to one more input; no new pattern, module, or layer. Resolution basis is a direct read of OwnerController.java plus a repository-wide grep for PageRequest.of (weaker than the IDE oracle, which is not connected in this run): exactly two call sites exist, OwnerController:135 and VetController:61, and no shared pagination helper. The only docs edit this dispatch made is REQ-OWNERSPAGEPARAM-001 joining the OwnerController Contracts row.
integration_points: GET /owners handled by OwnerController.processFindForm; the page parameter reaches both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (as the zero-based query index) and addPaginationModel (as the currentPage model attribute)

patterns.description: @RequestParam(defaultValue = "1") int page — the existing convention that the page parameter is one-based at the web boundary and converted to a zero-based index at the query

risks.risk: Clamping inside findPaginatedForOwnersLastName alone fixes the HTTP 500 but leaves addPaginationModel publishing the raw requested page as currentPage. templates/owners/ownersList.html drives the whole pagination widget off currentPage, so a request for page 0 would render the first page's rows with no current-page marker and a next link pointing back at the page already shown.
risks.mitigation: Normalize the page once, before it is used for either the query or the model, so both see the same effective page number.

risks.risk: VetController:61 carries the identical shape and is explicitly out of scope for this slice, so the defect survives in the vet directory after this fix lands.
risks.mitigation: None in this slice by design. Recorded here so the divergence is visible; docs/prd.md holds it as an open question. Not a refactor-first trigger — extracting a shared clamp across two independent feature packages has no behavioural justification while only one of them is in scope, and owner and vet do not reference each other (system-design.md Package Structure).

notes: Five-signal foundational check: none tripped. system-design.md is populated and partly human-confirmed, ADRs record the language, framework, and architecture shape, docs/ubiquitous-language.md is written and confirmed, the web-boundary input concern already has a recorded project-level pattern (controller-held checks plus bean validation), and no new bounded context appears. Autofix audit: the log holds no design-doc-autofix records; skipped. Boundary check against durable memory: no ADR or Non-Goals row speaks to page-range handling, so nothing here conflicts. The fix shape stays the implementer's call — this record names the constraint (one effective page number feeding both the query and the view), not the expression.

author: code-quality-reviewer
recommendations: `@RequestParam(defaultValue = "1")` duplicates the `FIRST_PAGE = 1` literal as a string annotation argument; the two can drift silently since annotation defaults can't reference the int constant directly. Consider a comment on `FIRST_PAGE` noting the annotation must be kept in sync, or a dedicated string constant for the annotation. Not blocking - low risk, purely a duplication note.
approved_aspects: `FIRST_PAGE` constant is well-named and documented with the one-based-page rationale inline
`pageToShow` is computed once at the top of `processFindForm` and threaded through both the query and the pagination model, so the two consumers of the page value can never disagree
`Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE)` is the simplest correct clamp for this rule; no manual branching needed
checkFormat passes clean on both changed files

author: test-reviewer
recommendations: The Javadoc on the two new parameterized tests (OwnerControllerTests.java:202-206) claims the assertions 'pin' the paged query rejecting a page index below zero, but the repository stub matches any(Pageable.class), so the tests never inspect the actual Pageable passed to findByLastNameStartingWith. The claim holds only because PageRequest.of(page-1,5) is real, unmocked production code that throws before the repository is reached. Tightening the stub to eq(PageRequest.of(0,5)) (or capturing the Pageable) in a future pass would make the assertion say what it means.
approved_aspects: Two @ParameterizedTest cases with @ValueSource(ints = {0,-1}) exercise both the listing and search paths, matching prd.md edge case 4 exactly ('A zero page and a negative page are each treated as the first page')
Method names theOwnerListingShouldShowTheFirstPageWhenThePageIsBelowTheFirst / theOwnerSearchShouldShowTheFirstPageWhenThePageIsBelowTheFirst follow the brief's the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD school

Tests exercise the real PageRequest.of(page-1, pageSize) construction in OwnerController rather than mocking it away, so a regression of the clamp (e.g. removing Math.max) would make PageRequest.of(-1, ...) throw and the test fail for a real reason, not a mock-satisfied one

Mocking stays within the brief's policy: MockitoBean on OwnerRepository is the pre-existing pattern in this file, consistent with the one sanctioned MockMvc web-boundary mock plus tolerated pre-existing repository stubbing
Test data (severalOwners, severalFranklins, pageBelowTheFirst) is named by role per the three-tier convention, no mystery literals
./gradlew test passes with the two new parameterized tests (4 executions) alongside the full existing OwnerControllerTests suite

VetController shares the identical unclamped page-index defect but is correctly left untested here; prd.md records it as an open question explicitly out of this change's scope, so the test surface matches the declared fix scope

author: change-grader
summary: clamp the owners page parameter to the first page

blast_radius.note: Four files in one module: eleven added lines confined to OwnerController.processFindForm, thirty-three test lines, and two docs edits (the row's two unknown_paths are docs/prd.md and docs/system-design.md, prose only). No sensitive paths, no schema, no config, no public API change.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every hunk: Math.max(page, FIRST_PAGE) is computed once and threaded to both consumers, findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel, so the query index and the rendered currentPage cannot diverge. No other use of the raw page parameter survives in the method, the empty-result, single-result and multi-result branches are untouched, and the pre-existing above-the-last-page behavior (an empty page falls to the notFound branch) is deliberately unchanged.

test_adequacy.note: Two parameterized tests cover both entry paths (bare listing and last-name search) at both boundary values 0 and -1, and assert the rendered view plus a currentPage of 1 rather than restating the implementation. They fail against the pre-fix code for a real reason: PageRequest.of(page-1, 5) is unmocked production code that throws on a negative index. The repository stub matches any Pageable, so the Pageable actually passed is never inspected; only a contrived two-divergent-clamps regression would slip through.

reviewer_hedging.note: All three planned reviewers approved with zero findings, and security-reviewer was scoped out by the review plan, so its null is expected rather than silence. But two of the three parked residual recommendations that reach the human only here: the code-quality reviewer flags the RequestParam defaultValue duplicating the FIRST_PAGE literal as a string that can drift silently, and the test reviewer flags the new tests Javadoc claiming to pin the paged query when the loose stub never inspects the Pageable.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions. The diff matches the triaged surface exactly: prd.md records the requirement, the done-when bullets, and edge case 4, and system-design.md adds the id to the OwnerController contracts row. The identical unclamped defect in the vet directory and the non-numeric page value are both left untouched and recorded as open questions rather than fixed opportunistically.

rationale: The clamp itself is sound and contained, and the tests fail against the pre-fix code for a real reason. What deserves the read is the residual polish two reviewers parked: a duplicated 1 literal in the RequestParam default that can drift from FIRST_PAGE, and a test Javadoc that overclaims what its loose stub verifies. Read those two notes, then merge.
